  `[advisories] ignore` entry with provenance and a closing condition.

  finding with a stated safe upgrade is upgraded at the source; the requirement restated to the advisory's floor where
  a direct dependency moves (wasmtime), a lockfile-only update elsewhere.

- **Prune, don't keep** (deny.toml :156–:159, :219–:222): a skip or ignore whose duplicate or advisory leaves the graph is
  removed in the same change, because cargo-deny flags it `unnecessary-skip` / `advisory-not-detected` and a stale entry
  hides the return.

- **Carve-out record shape** (deny.toml `ureq` :162–:170, `core-foundation` :178–:188): origin of the duplicate, why it is
  not source-fixable, owner, closing condition.

- **npm no-forward-fix exception** (npm-policy.json): GHSA-scoped, `reason` naming the chains and the rejected downgrade,
  `owner` = the chunk marker, `closing_condition` ending «prune when the gate runs green without this entry».
- **Distinct ids, never blocks** (security-plan §Dependency Security): the counts above are distinct `RUSTSEC-` / GHSA ids.

- **Measure, then apply and re-audit** (npm): `fixAvailable` is resolver output; the residual after the applied update is
  the truth (session learning 2026-08-30, rules/security.md).

body:
_Generated by /andromeda-phase P4. Read by /andromeda-implement. Manual edits between runs are fine; do not
edit during an /implement run._
- **Marker:** 2026-11-03-advisories-since-2026-10-12-closed · **Version:** andromeda-pulse-0.4.0 · **Generated:** 2026-11-03T20:45:00Z

The CI `supply-chain` job has been red on every push since 2026-10-12 on `cargo audit` alone (`ci#41582102601` on
`4080303a`): 42 vulnerabilities over 38 distinct ids, plus unsound warnings with stated upgrades, in crates this
project did not touch. This chunk closes every one of them by upgrade, as security-plan §Dependency Security requires
of a finding with a stated safe upgrade, and gives the no-solution findings a visible, ID-scoped disposition. Every
Rust upgrade fits the manifests' current requirements, so the change is a lockfile update plus wasmtime's
requirement restated to its advisories' floor (the 2026-10-04 precedent, arch §Stack and Technologies, Plugin runtime
row). Two of the updates are the founder's own word (`inputs#I2`): duckdb / libduckdb-sys 1.10505.0 → 1.10506.1, which
takes zip 6 → 9 as a build dependency on the DuckDB 1.5.x line, and tauri-plugin-updater 2.10.1 → 2.14.1, which takes
zip 4 → 9 and Tauri 2.11.0 → 2.12.5 with it.

With the audit green, the job's later steps run again, and the npm supply-chain gate among them is already red at HEAD
(22 GHSA findings, research §Sweeps). By the scope's boundary clause those findings are this chunk's too: 19 close by
in-range lockfile updates, and the three with no forward fix in their holders' ranges (minimatch, glob, zod, all
dev-only) take GHSA-scoped exceptions in `pulse-app/ui/npm-policy.json`, again the founder's word (`inputs#I2`). The
three no-solution unmaintained Rust ids of the zbus family take ID-scoped `deny.toml` ignore entries with provenance
(`inputs#I2`). No product behaviour changes. `multiple-versions = "deny"`, the tonic canary, keyring's four platform
features, the 1.95 toolchain pin and the Cranelift-only backend all stand (per security-plan §Dependency Security,
arch §Stack and Technologies, test-plan §9).

1. **wasmtime to 48.0.8.** In `Cargo.toml`, set the wasmtime requirement `"48.0.4"` → `"48.0.8"`, the floor
   RUSTSEC-2026-0422 / -0423 / -0424 state on the 48 line, and extend the provenance comment block above it (:108–:128)
   with one dated paragraph naming RUSTSEC-2026-0353 … -0359, -0361 … -0364, -0378, -0379, -0422, -0423, -0424, their
   stated ranges (`>=48.0.8, <49.0.0` on the 48 line) and that 49.x still needs rustc 1.96. Then `cargo update -p
   wasmtime` so the lockfile resolves 48.0.8 with cranelift 0.135.8 and pulley 48.0.8 (research §Sweeps, the dry run).

2. **The in-range Rust updates.** `cargo update -p rustls -p rustls-webpki -p quinn-proto -p webpki-root-certs -p
   pulldown-cmark -p zstd -p tokio -p event-listener`, plus `cargo update -p webpki-roots@1.0.7` (two webpki-roots
   versions stand). Expected lockfile reading, each a prediction to be measured: rustls 0.23.46, rustls-webpki 0.103.16,
   quinn-proto 0.11.19 (adding rand / rand_core 0.10, chacha20 0.10, rand_pcg 0.10), webpki-roots 1.0.11,
   webpki-root-certs 1.0.11, pulldown-cmark 0.13.6, zstd 0.13.4 with zstd-safe 7.4.0 and zstd-sys 2.1.2, tokio 1.54.1,
   event-listener 5.4.2. No manifest line changes for these.

3. **The DuckDB path (founder's word, `inputs#I2` item 1).** `cargo update -p duckdb --precise 1.10506.1`, which moves
   libduckdb-sys with it and zip 6.0.0 → 9.3.0 (predicted additions: nix 0.31.3, typed-path 0.13.0). The `Cargo.toml`
   requirement `"1.10500"` is unchanged; no `--precise` past the 1.5.x line (libduckdb-sys 1.20000.x is DuckDB 2.0).

4. **The updater path (founder's word, `inputs#I2` item 2).** `cargo update -p tauri-plugin-updater --precise 2.14.1`,
   which takes tauri 2.11.0 → 2.12.5, tauri-build / -codegen / -macros 2.6.0 → 2.7.4, tao 0.35.0 → 0.37.2 and about
   60 lockfile moves (research §Sweeps), and removes the five unic-* crates, phf 0.11 and png 0.17. The manifests'
   `tauri = "2.11"`, `tauri-build = "2.6"` and `tauri-plugin-updater = "2"` already admit these; none is restated.
   The plugin's one use site, `pulse-app/src/main.rs:303` (`tauri_plugin_updater::Builder::new().build()`), is the
   2.x surface at 2.14.1. If the build shows a forced API change anywhere, it is fixed at that site and recorded as an
   out-of-list edit, with no behaviour change.

5. **Re-read the audit.** `cargo audit` must exit 0 with no vulnerability. Read its id lines (`ID:        RUSTSEC-…`):
   none of the 38 vulnerability ids remains, nor RUSTSEC-2026-0386 (tokio), -0221 (event-listener) or the ten zstd-safe
   unsound ids. The warnings left are the zbus family's three unmaintained ids, the standing unmaintained set
   (bincode, paste, proc-macro-error, the GTK3 / glib stack) and any yanked crate. An id the run prints that is outside
   the HEAD set of research §Sweeps is new: stop and report it.

6. **`deny.toml` — prune, then add only what the graph needs.** Run `cargo deny check bans licenses sources` and
   `cargo deny check advisories` and act on what they print, in the existing record shape (research §Patterns):
   - prune every `[bans] skip` cargo-deny reports `unnecessary-skip` (predicted: `zip`, since both paths now resolve
     one zip 9.3.0; possibly `phf*`, `png`, `ctor` after the Tauri bump — record what it measures);
   - prune the five unic-* `[advisories] ignore` entries (RUSTSEC-2025-0075 / -0080 / -0081 / -0098 / -0100), whose
     closing condition fires once tauri-utils moves to urlpattern 0.6, if cargo-deny reports them
     `advisory-not-detected`;
   - add, for each new duplicate `multiple-versions` reports, an ID-scoped skip with origin, why it is not
     source-fixable, owner (this marker) and closing condition (predicted: `nix` 0.29 + 0.31, from zip 9);
   - add three ID-scoped `[advisories] ignore` entries, RUSTSEC-2026-0371 (zbus_names), -0370 (zvariant) and -0372
     (zvariant_derive), under one provenance comment: unmaintained, no stated solution; held through zbus 4.4.0 ←
     secret-service 4.0.0 ← keyring's `sync-secret-service` (the corpus key's Linux backend, which must not be
     dropped) and zbus 5.15.0 ← notify-rust ← tauri-plugin-notification; owner this marker; closing condition: a
     maintained replacement reaches those holders, or the holders leave the graph (the founder's word, `inputs#I2`
     item 3).
   `multiple-versions = "deny"` and the `tonic` deny canary are untouched; no skip names tonic.

7. **The npm channel — in-range updates.** In `pulse-app/ui`, update the 19 findings' packages inside their
   dependents' ranges: vite (direct, `^7.0.0`) to its patched 7.x, vitest / @vitest/mocker to their patched 4.x,
   undici, follow-redirects, qs, seroval and ip-address by targeted `npm update {pkg}`, after confirming each patched
   release exists with `npm view {pkg} versions` (session learning 2026-08-30, rules/security.md). `npm audit fix`
   without `--force` may do the same; never `--force`, never a downgrade. Then re-run `cargo xtask
   check:npm-supply-chain` and take its residual as the truth: the expected residual is exactly the three findings of
   step 8. Any other residual finding is a stop: report it, never except it.

8. **The npm channel — three exceptions (founder's word, `inputs#I2` item 4).** Add three `advisory_exceptions` to
   `pulse-app/ui/npm-policy.json` in its existing form (`ghsa · package · reason · owner · closing_condition · added`):
   GHSA-g3hv-75wg-m249 (minimatch; fixed ≥ 11.0.1; held at 3.x by eslint 9, @eslint/*, eslint-plugin-react and
   -jsx-a11y, at 9.x by @wdio/config, at 10.x by @typescript-eslint/typescript-estree and readdir-glob; no holder's
   latest release uses 11, eslint 10 included), GHSA-3g3m-2fjr-6pw4 (glob; @wdio/config's glob 10.5.0; its latest uses
   ^13, still in range; globby's glob 7 is outside the advisory) and GHSA-mrhx-c7xc-m3w5 (zod 3.25.76 under
   chromium-bidi; only a newer chromium-bidi through puppeteer-core majors reaches zod 4). Each `reason` names the dev-only
   chains and the rejected downgrade, `owner` this marker, `closing_condition` ending «prune when the gate runs green
   without this entry». `package.json` changes only if step 7's update needs it.

9. **Run the gate set** of `## Test Commands` in order: the manifest and lockfile reads, the standard gates
   (capability-drift before the workspace run), the bindings regen as the last cargo-adjacent step with its close
   against the chunk base, the webview gates (the npm lockfile changed), the window boot series (Tauri moved), the
   console engine cycle (DuckDB, tokio and rustls moved) and the local pre-push check.
- none
- `Cargo.toml` — the wasmtime requirement and its provenance comment (step 1)
- `Cargo.lock` — steps 1–4
- `deny.toml` — pruned skips and ignores, new ID-scoped skip(s) and the three zbus-family ignores (step 6)
- `pulse-app/ui/package-lock.json` — the in-range npm updates (step 7)
- `pulse-app/ui/package.json` — only where step 7's update requires it
- `pulse-app/ui/npm-policy.json` — the three exceptions (step 8)

The window boot smoke runs: Tauri 2.11.0 → 2.12.5 and tao 0.35.0 → 0.37.2 move the window runtime (the boot self-end
closed at 2026-10-10 was measured against tao 0.35's device-event thread, obs-plan history). The console engine's
runtime gate is one engine cycle, since DuckDB, tokio and rustls move under it (obs-plan §10: a lockfile-only DuckDB
bump has changed runtime behaviour before). The webview gates run because `pulse-app/ui/package-lock.json` changes. No
procedure is added or changed, so the bindings close is the procedure-preserving form: `capability-drift` before the
workspace run, the regen as the last cargo-adjacent step, then `git diff --quiet` against the chunk base (test-plan §3).
No headful self-verify is listed: `cargo xtask self-verify` drives WebView2 through `msedgedriver` on a Windows host,
and this Linux host has none; the boot series and the CI a11y job stand in for the UI half. `cargo xtask test:a11y` is
not a local entry (the Playwright headless shell is not installed on this host, measured at the previous chunk's P5);
the CI `a11y` job runs it with its regression detector and is read by name in the CI read, and locally the suite's
config-named `--list` entry guards against a list-time import failure. `cargo auditable build --workspace --release`
is the CI `supply-chain` job's last step and is read there. Lean checks per `inputs#I1`: the gates this plan requires,
each run once.
The chunk base is `0e13e255b4c56026d656a535834f3d623678060e`, HEAD when this plan was written.

- **[Plugin Runtime] WASM Component Model via `wasmtime` 25+ (requirement `"48.0.8"`, lockfile-resolved 48.0.8 as of 2026-11-03) with WIT interfaces**: capability-based sandboxing (no syscalls, file, or socket access unless explicitly granted) and type-safe host imports match the standards path. Extism was considered for easier multi-language guest support, but Component Model is the standards-track choice the input.md explicitly calls out and aligns with Bytecode Alliance LTS.

- Plugin runtime: `wasmtime` 25+ Component Model with WIT interfaces (requirement `"48.0.8"`, lockfile-resolved 48.0.8 as of 2026-11-03), capability-scoped. The Tauri-side capability `pulse:plugin-fs` gates the host's read of `~/.andromeda-pulse/plugins/` for module discovery and is independent of the per-guest WIT capability grants (which never include host filesystem unless a plugin's WIT explicitly imports a fs interface).

SQLite was rejected because aggregating 10k spans/sec into per-service p99 series in row-store SQL turns the query into the bottleneck. - **[Corpus Write Arbitration — which of two writers to the same incident row wins] Monotonic last-writer guard at the `CorpusWriter` choke point**: incident status writes are arbitrated by a bound `AND updated_unix_nano <= ?2` predicate appended to the existing `incidents` UPDATE, with a second bound `SELECT 1 FROM incidents WHERE id = ?1` classifying the zero-row result. `CorpusWriter::update_incident_status` and `IncidentPersistence::update_incident_status` therefore return `Result<IncidentWriteOutcome, _>` (`Applied` | `DeclinedStale`): a write whose payload is OLDER than the stored row is **DECLINED, not failed** — losing to a fresher writer is an expected outcome, and encoding it as an `Error` would make "log it as a failure" the default at every call site. `Error::QueryFailed` continues to mean the row does not exist. The predicate works because every registry mutator bumps `updated_at_unix_nano` to `now` (`mark_resolved` / `mark_read` / `attach_resolution_summary` / `attach_interpretation_summary`), so a stale snapshot necessarily carries a smaller value. **Placement is the corpus layer, not the `triage` trait**, because it is the ONLY choke point all SEVEN production writers traverse: six share `IncidentPersistence` (the persist cycle, the auto-resolve observer, `incidents.acknowledge`, `incidents.mark_resolved`, and both `inference_runtime` L4 writers) while the seventh — the `crates/mcp-server/src/tools.rs` incident-resolve write (`dispatch_mark_incident_resolved` → `update_incident_status`) — calls `CorpusWriter` directly and bypasses that trait entirely. Its one carrier is the console engine's door, in the engine's own process, over the engine's own `Arc<dyn CorpusWriter>`, refused with `-32001` before the dispatcher is called unless the write switch `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DOOR_RESOLVE` reads on — so the seventh writer traverses this choke point, and the guard, its existence probe and `Applied` / `DeclinedStale` are unchanged (`the_door_resolves_an_incident_and_says_it_was_a_write`, `pulse-app/tests/integration_engine_boot.rs`, reads the row `resolved` through the engine's own `CorpusWriter`). The placement costs no new crate edge (`mcp-server → corpus` and `pulse-app → corpus` already exist) and no DDL. **REJECTED — a status-only predicate** (`status != 'resolved'`): disproved by measurement, since `attach_resolution_summary` REQUIRES `status == Resolved` and is the documented final write, so such a guard would break it. **REJECTED — delta-persistence** (persist only changed rows): larger, needs new dirty-tracking state with crash-loss semantics, and does nothing for the cross-process path, which is not a snapshot problem. `triage::contract::IncidentWriteOutcome` is a deliberate PARALLEL type rather than a re-export — `triage` sits below `corpus` in the dependency DAG, so the `pulse-app` adapter maps between the two. **Residual CLOSED 2026-08-29** (chunk `2026-08-29-app-registry-reconciliation`): this entry previously recorded an accepted residual — the guard made the CORPUS correct but not the app, so after an external MCP resolve the running app showed the incident active until restart and its persist cycle declined that row every cycle. That is no longer true. The 60 s incident persist cycle now RECONCILES first: it reads the durable active-incident **ids** for the workspace through `triage::contract::DurableActiveIncidents::active_incident_ids` (a narrow read port declared in `triage`, implemented at the `pulse-app` binary boundary over the SAME `Arc<dyn CorpusWriter>` the write path uses, so no new crate edge and no payload decoded in `triage`), resolves any registry row absent from that set via the existing `IncidentRegistry::mark_resolved` transition, and only then runs its write loop — so the row it just reconciled is never re-offered. A durable-read `Err` reconciles NOTHING (treating it as an empty set would match every registry row and resolve the whole active list) and warns on `triage.incident.persist.error` with `persist_kind = "incident_reconcile"`; the outcome is counted once per cycle as `reconciled_count` on `triage.incident.persist`. `load_active_incidents` remains a boot-only caller, and the monotonic predicate, its existence probe and the `Applied` / `DeclinedStale` semantics above are unchanged. Measured live: a real `andromeda-pulse-mcp` subprocess resolved a row and the running app dropped it within two persist cycles with NO restart (`reconciled_count` 1 / `declined_count` 0, against 0 / 2 under a mutation with reconciliation removed). The reconciler deliberately emits no `IncidentLifecycleEvent`: `pulse://stream/incidents` has producers but no consumer, so a send would be dead plumbing — the webview learns of the change through its existing ~1 s `incidents.list_active` poll.

- **Engine door — the tools inside the engine's process** (chunk 2026-10-10-door-inside-the-engine-s-process; the form an outside reader depends on — Conductor reads the engine through it): **Connect** — a Unix-domain stream socket at `run/door/sock` under the data dir of a running `andromeda-pulse-engine run`, as the engine's own account. **Admission** — on every accepted connection the peer's account is read from the kernel and must equal the engine's effective account; any other account, root included, and a peer whose account cannot be read, sees the connection closed with no byte written. **Call** — one JSON-RPC 2.0 object per line, UTF-8, at most 65 536 bytes; a request with no `id` is not answered and runs nothing. Methods: `initialize` (`jsonrpc::initialize_result()` unchanged — `serverInfo.name` reads `andromeda-pulse-mcp`, protocol `2024-11-05`) · `tools/list` · `tools/call` · `ping`. `tools/call` carries `params.name` and `params.arguments` and runs one of the nine tools of the entry above through `mcp_server::tools::call_tool` over the engine's own handles — a read connection of the door's own taken from the engine's buffer connection, the engine's `Arc<dyn CorpusWriter>` and its `incident_workspace_key`; the door opens no database and no corpus, reads no `run/workspace-key` and prepares no SQL. `arguments` must be an object whose every member the tool's `inputSchema.properties` declares, else `-32602` before any tool runs. **The one write** — `mark_incident_resolved` answers `-32001` unless `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DOOR_RESOLVE` reads on; `tools/list` names it either way, marked `write`. **Answer** — one line, `result` as the tool returns it, at most 1 048 576 bytes; a longer answer is not cut, the caller gets `-32003`. **Bounds** — a request line over 65 536 bytes: `-32600`, the connection closed · a call over 5 s: `-32002`, and the door interrupts its own read connection · a connection with no complete line for 30 s, or a caller that does not read its answer, is closed · at most 8 connections, a ninth closed at accept · one tool call at a time. **Errors** — the JSON-RPC error object with a fixed message, never the tool's own text: `-32700` parse error · `-32600` request too large · `-32601` unknown tool / method not found · `-32602` invalid arguments · `-32603` tool failed · `-32001` the write is switched off · `-32002` timed out · `-32003` answer too large. So "no such incident" and a fault both read `-32603`. **Records** — `app.boot.door`, `door.call`, `door.refused`, closed labels only (obs-plan §6 and §8 hold their fields). Not shown: that the interrupt ends a real running query (no query of that chunk runs long enough). **Stdio** (since chunk 2026-10-12-stdio-agent-reaches-the-door) — a caller with no socket client reaches the door by starting `andromeda-pulse-engine door` as the engine's own account. The relay resolves the data dir as `run` does (`engine_boot::resolve_data_dir()`) and canonicalizes the data dir and `{data dir}/run/door/sock` both sides; a socket that does not resolve, resolves outside the data dir, or has a path of 108 bytes or more is unreachable. Each standard-input line that is not whitespace alone takes a connection of its own, in order: the line is sent with its `\n` (an unterminated last line gets one), the write side shut, the whole answer read until the door closes, and only then written to standard output unchanged — the `tools/list` line through the relay equals a direct socket read byte for byte. A line over 65 536 bytes is sent as its first 65 537 bytes with no terminator and the rest of it discarded, never sent. The relay parses nothing, writes no answer of its own, retries nothing and has no time bound of its own; it writes no record and no file. Standard input ending is exit 0; a connect, write, shutdown or read failure on the socket, or a failed write of standard output, is exit 1 with the one fixed standard-error line `andromeda-pulse-engine door: the door cannot be reached` and nothing on standard output from the failed connection; off Unix the word prints that line and exits 1 at once. The door treats the relay as any caller: the account check, one `door.call` per answered request, a request with no `id` answered and recorded with nothing, no idle refusal (one connection per request). Another account through the relay receives no byte: on Linux a refused connection reads `EPIPE` or `ECONNRESET` at the client, so the relay exits 1 with the fixed line (as measured on `ci#38227488889`). The door's own form above is unchanged. Console program only, Unix only, in every build.

The console program's `door` word (the stdio relay, chunk `2026-10-12-stdio-agent-reaches-the-door`) has no sink at all — no subscriber, no record — its stdout reserved for the door's JSON-RPC answer lines and its stderr for one fixed line on exit 1

| Storage engine | DuckDB 1.5.x via the `duckdb` crate — Cargo.toml requirement `1.10500` (caret, untouched), lockfile-resolved **1.10506.1** | Embedded columnar OLAP, in-memory ring buffer (5–10 min, configurable) |

| Plugin runtime | `wasmtime` 25+ family with WASM Component Model + WIT — Cargo.toml requirement `"48.0.8"`, lockfile-resolved **48.0.8** (Cranelift 0.135.8); the bump from 48.0.5 closed the wasmtime advisory ids open at 48.0.5 with no advisory ignore (the earlier bumps: from 48.0.3, closing RUSTSEC-2026-0325 / -0326 / -0327; from 46.0.3, closing RUSTSEC-2026-0316), and 49.x is out of reach while the toolchain is pinned at 1.95 (49.0.2, the first patched 49.x, needs Rust 1.96) | Capability-scoped third-party extensions loaded from `~/.andromeda-pulse/plugins/` |

- **[Database] DuckDB embedded via the `duckdb` crate — requirement `1.10500` (caret) in Cargo.toml, lockfile-resolved 1.10506.1 (DuckDB 1.5.x bundled), in-memory ring buffer**: columnar+SQL+Arrow trifecta is exactly what aggregating spans/metrics by service/time-bucket needs at 10k spans/sec. SQLite was rejected because aggregating 10k spans/sec into per-service p99 series in row-store SQL turns the query into the bottleneck. DataFusion remains a documented swap-out only if DuckDB's C++ FFI complicates Tauri cross-compile.

- **[Plugin Runtime] WASM Component Model via `wasmtime` 25+ (requirement `"48.0.8"`, lockfile-resolved 48.0.8) with WIT interfaces**: capability-based sandboxing (no syscalls, file, or socket access unless explicitly granted) and type-safe host imports match the standards path. Extism was considered for easier multi-language guest support, but Component Model is the standards-track choice the input.md explicitly calls out and aligns with Bytecode Alliance LTS.
- Database: DuckDB 1.5.x via the `duckdb` crate — requirement `1.10500` (caret), lockfile-resolved 1.10506.1 — in-memory ring buffer (5–10 min retention, configurable).

- Plugin runtime: `wasmtime` 25+ Component Model with WIT interfaces (requirement `"48.0.8"`, lockfile-resolved 48.0.8), capability-scoped. The Tauri-side capability `pulse:plugin-fs` gates the host's read of `~/.andromeda-pulse/plugins/` for module discovery and is independent of the per-guest WIT capability grants (which never include host filesystem unless a plugin's WIT explicitly imports a fs interface).

**Section:** §1 Obs Scope Summary (the CLI row, the P3 row) · §4 Span / Trace Coverage (the door row) · §6 Log Coverage (the `warn` row) · PII Scrubbing (the door's three leaves) · Universal (agent-driven specific) (the relay's stdout rule) · Project-specific (andromeda-pulse) (the nine tools' guard rule) · obs-plan/contracts/logging-stack (Sink)
**Change:**
- The CLI row's `door` word: «(the stdio relay, `pulse_app::door_bridge`)» (was «…; PROVISIONAL with the door's item, §4 Scenario P3»).
- The P3 row points to «§4 Scenario P3, which holds the door's item sentence» (was «…the door's PROVISIONAL sentence»).
- The door row in §4 Span / Trace Coverage, the `warn` row's door records (`app.boot.door`, `door.call`, `door.refused`), the PII door leaves and the nine tools' guard rule each drop their «PROVISIONAL — §4 Scenario P3» mark; the relay's stdout rule and the logging-stack Sink's `door` word each drop «PROVISIONAL with the door's item».
- The rest of each fact is unchanged.
**Why:** the door's one item is ratified (the entry above: the founder's word of 2026-11-02 on shaping-0.4.0 items 27 and 28, relayed by overseer1, read by the pc-overseer as the whole door item), so every pointer to its PROVISIONAL status in this plan and its key file drops.
**Kept:** the pre-push sixth stage's PROVISIONAL marks stay — a separate item, not the door's; the ruling dropped the door's marks only.
**Ref:** .andromeda/runs/2026-11-03T21-56-11Z-wrap/

- **MCP server:** spec-fixed JSON-RPC 2.0 method names — `initialize`, `tools/list`, `tools/call`, `ping` (a request with no `id` answered with nothing). Tool methods (9): `query_traces`, `query_metrics`, `query_logs`, `generate_snapshot`, `query_incident_list`, `retrieve_report`, `retrieve_telemetry_slice`, `mark_incident_resolved` (these 4 chunk #94), `retrieve_incident_events` (chunk 2026-10-02-incident-events-readable-through-mcp). The wire is the console engine's door — line-delimited JSON-RPC 2.0 over the Unix-domain socket `run/door/sock`, methods `initialize` · `tools/list` · `tools/call` · `ping` (arch §Standard Contracts → Engine door). That wire is reached over stdio through the relay `andromeda-pulse-engine door`, one connection per request.

The toolchain is pinned to rustc 1.95.0 and the workspace declares `rust-version = "1.95"` once in `[workspace.package]`, equal to the pin and set by the resolved dependency graph (wasmtime and its internal crates, cranelift and pulley declare 1.95.0, as measured on wasmtime 48.0.5; not re-read on the resolved wasmtime 48.0.8, which the pinned 1.95.0 toolchain builds with `declared_floor_equals_the_pinned_channel` passing) — no toolchain below 1.95.0 builds the product, though the workspace's own code needs only rustc ≥ 1.89. The xtask test `declared_floor_equals_the_pinned_channel` holds the declared floor equal to the pin. Edition 2024 itself cannot parse below 1.85.0 (security-plan keeps that as the floor never to drift below); wasmtime 49.x is out of reach while the pin is 1.95 (it needs Rust 1.96).

- Write surface (`CorpusWriter`): incident status writes are arbitrated at the `CorpusWriter` choke point by the monotonic last-writer guard (`Applied` | `DeclinedStale`), which all SEVEN production writers traverse — six through `triage::contract::IncidentPersistence` (the persist cycle, the auto-resolve observer, `incidents.acknowledge`, `incidents.mark_resolved`, both `inference_runtime` L4 writers) and the seventh, the `mark_incident_resolved` tool calling `CorpusWriter` directly, whose one carrier is the console engine's door, in the engine's own process, over the engine's own `Arc<dyn CorpusWriter>` and only when the write switch `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DOOR_RESOLVE` is on; the guard is unchanged. No baseline snapshot is written here: `baseline_state` is dropped.
- `duckdb` crate — requirement `1.10500` (caret), lockfile-resolved 1.10506.1 (DuckDB 1.5.x bundled) — embedded columnar OLAP, in-memory `:memory:` connection.

the `boot` job's `Console engine cycle` step uploads that dir's whole `logs/` as `logs-engine-Linux` — the engine's log family plus `boot.log` and `build.log`, the last holding the runner's checkout paths and passing no scrubber, as the boot upload's does; the dev example `inject_demo` (never shipped) reads `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_OTLP_GRPC_PORT` to pick its port, the host fixed at `127.0.0.1`, a value that is no port refused with exit 2 and never repeated. **The exit-witness arm since chunk `2026-10-10-boot-smoke-s-self-end-named-from-a-run` — classification PROVISIONAL** (the operator's reading of 2026-10-10, the pc overseer: routine harness evidence, the app's exit record; awaiting the founder's own word at the epoch boundary; not the founder's word): bare `scripts/agent-run.sh boot`, the window program's boot, alone among the script's paths reads `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_EXIT_WITNESS_LIB` (sh only; since chunk `2026-10-10-agent-harness-drives-the-console-engine` the script holds a second spawn line, the console engine's under `boot engine`, which never reads the variable, sets no preload and neither removes nor creates the witness file; trimmed; unset or blank spawns the app as before; a regular file is loaded onto the window app's spawn command through `LD_PRELOAD`, with `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_EXIT_WITNESS_FILE` = `{data dir}/logs/exit-witness.jsonl` beside it, neither exported; set and not a regular file is `boot: exit witness library not found`, exit 1, before the pre-build — FAIL CLOSED, not the class's clean skip). The library (`scripts/exit-witness.c`) is the one harness member that runs INSIDE the app's process: it interposes `exit` / `_exit` / `_Exit` / `quick_exit` / `abort`, removes both variables from the process environment at load so no process the app starts loads it, is inert without its file, and applies no check of its own to the path; no `pulse-app` code reads either variable. It runs inside the window app's process only, never the console engine's. One more harness member reads the variable since chunk `2026-10-10-agent-harness-drives-the-console-engine`: `cargo xtask harness:engine-cycle` reads it by value only to pass it on into its children's cleared environment when present, prints and writes nothing of it, reports the cycle data dir's `logs/exit-witness.jsonl` as the closed label `witness_file` = `absent` | `present`, and reads `fail` on `present`; no classification of its own is made for that reader. Kept under the data dir's `logs/`, harness-written, never read by the product: `exit-witness.jsonl` (closed line shapes — pids, a thread id, a process name, the call, its code, `errno`, frames as module basename · exported symbol · offset; it passes no scrubber; `harness:settled` reads it under a bound and lets one closed label out, `exit_witness`), `boot-series.json` and the `series/boot-{ordinal}/` per-boot copies; `cargo xtask harness:boot-series` reads `PATH` by value only to find `xvfb-run` and sets `XDG_DATA_HOME` / `XDG_CACHE_HOME` on each of its boots; since chunk `2026-10-10-boot-smoke-s-self-end-closed` it is also a second reader of the witness file — for a boot that took no settle verdict (and the smoke's top data dir when it holds no `logs/harness-settled.json`) it reads that boot's `run/andromeda-pulse.spawn`, `run/andromeda-pulse.exit` and `logs/exit-witness.jsonl` through the existing bounded readers and lists the exit record and one closed label as that boot's `ended` / `exit_witness`; no member, label, kept file or line kind added, nothing new read from inside the app's process, and the second reader is part of the same PROVISIONAL item as the record itself (the operator's word at that chunk's wrap: one thing awaits the founder's word, not two). The operator's standing stop: every kept witness file is read whole, and a line holding anything beyond its shape stops the reading. **NARROWED EXCEPTION (guard landed 2026-08-26, chunk `2026-08-26-l4-runtime-security-residuals`) — the rule is still NOT categorical, but it is no longer a convention:** `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_MODEL_PATH` · `_LLAMA_CUDA_BIN_PATH` · `_LLAMA_CPU_BIN_PATH` are read by a SHIPPED binary — the window app `pulse-app` alone; the console program `andromeda-pulse-engine` reads none of them and no `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_L4_ALLOW_ROOT`, constructs no `LlamaCliInference` and emits no `interpretation.model.*` record, so the residual below does not reach it (`pulse-app/src/llamacli_inference.rs::validate_path_input`), so the harness carve-out does not reach them. **Always-on now:** trim + reject-empty · reject a `..` traversal component BEFORE canonicalizing (canonicalization erases `..`, so a post-check can never see it) · reject over `MAX_PATH_INPUT_BYTES` (4096) · `canonicalize()` · assert regular-file. **Confinement is OPT-IN** via `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_L4_ALLOW_ROOT`, comparing the canonicalized candidate against the canonicalized root — **both sides canonicalized**, because Windows `canonicalize()` yields a `\\?\` prefix and a one-sided compare fails regardless of the true relationship. A root that is SET but unresolvable **fails closed** (every candidate rejected), so a typo cannot silently disable the guard. Opt-in rather than data-dir-default because the GGUF and `llama-cli.exe` live outside the data dir BY DESIGN — a default would reject every configuration that has run L4. **Residual consequence, scoped:** on a host that leaves the root unset, an actor who can set these vars can still point the product at an arbitrary on-disk file — read as a model, or EXECUTED as the inference binary. Accepted under this tier's local-single-user trust boundary, and no longer silent: the unconfined posture emits one WARN per boot on `interpretation.model.allow_root`. **The primitive here — and now project-wide — is `std` both-sides-canonicalize on the `publish_workspace_key` precedent** (`strict-path` declined at the 2026-08-26 P4 review, then dropped from the graph at `2026-08-29-advisory-backlog`). The sibling argv-prompt residual is CLOSED: `validate_prompt_bounded` bounds the `-p` value before `Command` assembly. **Ratified carve-out — the corpus-key lock dir (chunk `2026-10-04-corpus-key-creation-is-race-free`; founder ratification 2026-10-04):** both product binaries (`pulse-app`, `andromeda-pulse-engine`) read the system `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` (Linux) through `Corpus::open` to place the content-free lock file `andromeda-pulse-corpus-key-{h16}.lock`; trimmed, then when set it must be absolute, `canonicalize()` and be a directory, else lock-dir resolution FAILS CLOSED (`KeychainError::Unavailable`, never a temp-dir fallback); unset/blank ⇒ the canonicalized `std::env::temp_dir()`. Data-dir confinement is omitted by design (the lock is keyed on the one per-user credential entry, shared by processes with different data dirs) — with the `~/Downloads` export sink and the per-spawn L4 grammar temp file in `std::env::temp_dir()` (since chunk #84; the committed GBNF since chunk `2026-10-05-l4-runs-the-founder-s-pick-with-its-authors-settings`) it is one of the THREE product-written locations outside the data dir. The L4 argv's other operands are first-party (founder-ratified 2026-10-05): the `--grammar-file` temp path holding the committed `L4_OUTPUT_GBNF` (`grammar_for_schema` refuses any other schema) and the sampling constants `--temp 1.0 --top-p 0.95 --top-k 64 --min-p 0` — `-p` stays the one OTLP-derived operand. A harness-only second reader of that bound (chunk `2026-10-07-l4-probe-reproduces-the-canary-history-miss`; a Boundary widening the founder answered 2026-10-07): the dev probe's `--replay` (`pulse-app/examples/l4_decision_probe/replay.rs`, an example binary, never shipped) passes a captured product prompt, read from a run-time path outside the tree, unchanged as its `-p` operand through the same `validate_prompt_bounded` and its own file checks (regular files, at most 64 KiB, UTF-8, a capture directory inside the work tree and outside `target/` refused); nothing of a prompt is printed, stored or committed, and the product's argv is unchanged.

_A boundary widening, one item, ratified: the endpoint, the owner check, the reach of the nine tools and of the one write, the write-switch variable, the workflow step that runs a client as a second account, the console program's third word `door` (the stdio relay) and the step's second arm (security-plan §Threat Model Summary → Attack surface, the door's vector)._

- The door is a Unix-domain stream socket at `{data dir}/run/door/sock` (mode 0600, inside `run/door/`, mode 0700), opened by `andromeda-pulse-engine run` alone; the window app seats none; no TCP port and no network listener is added. The path is canonicalized, refused when it leaves the data dir, and must be shorter than 108 bytes; a door that cannot bind leaves the engine running with no door. Since chunk `2026-10-12-stdio-agent-reaches-the-door` the console program's third word `door` is the stdio relay to a running engine's door (a boundary widening, part of this item, ratified): it boots no engine (neither `engine_boot::init_process` nor `engine_boot::start`), resolves the data dir through `engine_boot::resolve_data_dir`, canonicalizes the data dir and `{data dir}/run/door/sock` both sides and treats a socket that does not resolve, resolves outside the data dir or has a path of 108 bytes or more as unreachable; it reads standard input by line bounded at `door::MAX_REQUEST_BYTES` + 1 (an over-bound line's rest discarded, never sent), parses no request and sends each line on a connection of its own, the door applying every bound and the account check; an unreachable door or a failed socket or standard-output operation is exit 1 with one fixed standard-error line and nothing on standard output; it adds no env var, flag, value, listener, port, file, pid file or log record.

- The `lint-test` step `Door refuses another account` (since chunk 2026-10-10-door-inside-the-engine-s-process; ratified with the door, test-plan §9) runs two arms of `integration_door` directly after `cargo xtask test` — `another_account_is_refused_at_each_of_three_layers` and, since chunk 2026-10-12-stdio-agent-reaches-the-door, `another_account_through_the_bridge_receives_nothing` (the relay word and the step's second arm ratified with the door), as a plain step with no soft-fail key, and passes only when nextest exits 0 and the kept output holds both arms' sentences — the three-layer sentence and the bridge sentence (`door bridge other-account arm: no byte reached another account through the bridge, the account check refused`). The three-layer arm's client (`python3 -c`) and the relay arm's copy of the built engine, run as `door`, both run under `sudo -n -u nobody` and `sudo -n`, so the runner must offer a second account by `sudo -n` and `python3`. A stated exception to "FAILS, never skips": where `sudo -n true` fails (the dev host) each of the two arms prints its skip sentence and passes; the CI step is what turns a skip red. Green on `ci#38097928056`, and again on `ci#38227488889` (chunk 2026-10-12-stdio-agent-reaches-the-door), where the relay's four other-account readings each exited 1 with 0 bytes on standard output. `pulse-app/tests/*.rs` counts 112 files (as measured at the work tree of chunk 2026-11-03-stdio-sidecar-retired) and the workspace run 3186 tests as of chunk 2026-10-12-stdio-agent-reaches-the-door (112 and 3174 at the door's chunk).

- **Unit tests (webview, since chunk #11):** `vitest` 4.x (4.1.12, as resolved by `pulse-app/ui/package-lock.json`; the vitest 3 mocker is vulnerable, GHSA-82fw) with `jsdom` 26 environment + `@testing-library/react` 16 for DOM-shape assertions on React 19 components. Co-located `*.test.tsx` adjacent to source under `pulse-app/ui/src/`. Emits JUnit XML to `target/junit-ui.xml` (matches `cargo-nextest --message-format junit` shape) for agent-driven discipline. Coverage gate scope: presentational components (e.g., `pulse-app/ui/src/components/icons/`) explicitly EXCLUDED at Foundation pre-shell stage; integration coverage applies via `tauri-driver` E2E from chunk #25 (webview shell). `vitest.config.mjs` lives at `pulse-app/ui/vitest.config.mjs` with `setupFiles: ["./src/test-setup.ts"]` registering `@testing-library/react` `afterEach(cleanup)`.

- **E2E OTLP gRPC:** `tonic` 0.14.5 native client → loopback `:4317`. **OTLP HTTP:** `reqwest` 0.12.x async + `axum-test` 18.7.0 → loopback `:4318`. **MCP tools (P3):** no stdio sidecar, no `mcp-server` feature and no env gate — a `tokio::net::UnixStream` client writes JSON-RPC 2.0 lines to the door of a spawned `andromeda-pulse-engine run` (`pulse-app/tests/e2e_p3_mcp_subprocess_tools_call.rs`; the door below). **Console engine program:** the built `andromeda-pulse-engine` spawned by `std::process::Command` from `pulse-app/tests/integration_console_engine.rs` under a cleared environment (no display variable, no session bus, its own TempDir data dir, two claimed loopback ports — since chunk 2026-10-10-engine-harness-proofs-completed a number from 20000 to 31999, 24317 and 24318 left out, held under an advisory file lock in `target/test-ports/`, never bound to 0 and released), its command grammar in process through `pulse-app/tests/unit_console_commands.rs`; the harness's own path to it is `cargo xtask harness:engine-cycle` on ports 24317 / 24318; and since that chunk the committed `scripts/agent-run.sh` and the built cycle verb are run with `bash` on a real console engine by the two `xtask/tests` binaries (`agent_run_shell`, `engine_cycle_refusals`), which need `bash`, a Linux `/proc` and the engine built in the test profile. **Console engine door (Unix only):** a `tokio::net::UnixStream` client at `{data dir}/run/door/sock` — over a stand-in `Tools` in process (`unit_door.rs`), the door seated by `engine_boot::start` in process (`integration_engine_boot.rs`) and a spawned `andromeda-pulse-engine run` (`integration_door.rs`) — and, since chunk 2026-10-12-stdio-agent-reaches-the-door, the stdio relay `andromeda-pulse-engine door` (`unit_door_bridge.rs` and two relay arms of `integration_door.rs`); the two other-account arms print a skip sentence and pass where `sudo -n true` fails, so the `lint-test` step `Door refuses another account` runs both on the runner and fails unless it reads both arms' sentences (ratified with the door).

```bash
# Run pulse-app (Tauri dev mode with hot reload)
cargo tauri dev

# Or direct
cargo run --bin pulse-app

# Console engine — the package's second program: same engine boot, no window, no display, no model runner
cargo build --bin andromeda-pulse-engine --release
target/release/andromeda-pulse-engine run        # stays up until SIGTERM / SIGINT; binds 4317 / 4318 by default and writes the same pid file as pulse-app
target/release/andromeda-pulse-engine version    # one line, exit 0; any other command line is usage, exit 2 (usage: andromeda-pulse-engine <run|version|door>)
target/release/andromeda-pulse-engine door       # Unix; the stdio relay to a running engine's run/door/sock, one connection per stdin line; boots no engine; exit 0 when stdin ends, 1 with one fixed stderr line when the door cannot be reached

# Override env
ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR=$TMPDIR/dev \
ANDROMEDA_PULSE_LOG_LEVEL=debug \
ANDROMEDA_PULSE_OTLP_GRPC_PORT=14317 \
ANDROMEDA_PULSE_OTLP_HTTP_PORT=14318 \
cargo run --bin pulse-app
```

body: - 2026-05-19: EXTENSION to the 2026-05-13 bindings.ts regen entry — the regen trigger is BROADER than `cargo nextest run`. Empirically verified at session 100 wrap: `cargo run --no-default-features` (invoked by `npx @tauri-apps/cli dev` during Phase 2b smoke check) ALSO overwrites `pulse-app/ui/src/bindings/index.ts` to the no-mcp shape — the wrap-time `cargo xtask capability-drift` re-check fired with 3 missing (`mcp.start` / `mcp.status` / `mcp.stop`) despite a clean state at /implement Phase 2 just minutes earlier. Root cause: `taurpc 0.7`'s `Router::into_handler()` triggers `export_types()` in dev mode any time it's called — that includes the production `main.rs` setup closure that runs when `cargo run` executes the binary, NOT just the `emit_taurpc_bindings` test. So the regen-via-mcp-server-feature recovery step (per 2026-05-17 HEAD-broken-state entry) must run AFTER any operation that builds + runs `pulse-app`'s `main.rs` under default features — including: (a) `cargo nextest run --workspace --profile ci` (per 2026-05-13), (b) `cargo nextest run -p pulse-app` (any test that triggers Router construction), (c) `cargo run -p pulse-app` (production launch), (d) `cargo tauri dev` or `npx @tauri-apps/cli dev` (Phase 2b smoke check). The wrap-session Phase 2 standard nextest re-verification followed by the smoke check sequence will leave bindings.ts in the broken state at wrap-time UNLESS the regen-via-mcp-server-feature explicitly fires after the LAST default-features cargo operation. Operational discipline: treat the regen-via-mcp-server-feature as the final pre-commit step at every wrap-session, ALWAYS pre-commit verified via `grep -c '"mcp":' pulse-app/ui/src/bindings/index.ts` ≥1 + `cargo xtask capability-drift` clean. Apply at every wrap with /implement chains involving multiple default-features cargo invocations (smoke checks + test reruns being the prime offenders). **[corrected 2026-11-03: the `mcp-server` feature, its `mcp.*` router and the `andromeda-pulse-mcp` sidecar left at chunk `2026-11-03-stdio-sidecar-retired` — every regenerating op now writes the one bindings shape, so the no-mcp shape, the `--features mcp-server` regen and the `grep -c '"mcp":'` probe no longer exist; the order that stands is test-plan's per-chunk gate discipline (`capability-drift` before the workspace run, the featureless `emit_taurpc_bindings` regen last, `git diff --quiet {chunk-base} -- pulse-app/ui/src/bindings/index.ts` closing), green at chunk `2026-11-03-advisories-since-2026-10-12-closed`]**

- 2026-06-12 (session 186): CRITICAL EXTENSION to the 2026-05-19 bindings.ts regen-discipline family — the regen verification MUST target the STAGED copy, and the regen must be re-sequenced AFTER `cargo llvm-cov`. Session 185's wrap adopted the testing.md "sequence llvm-cov last-and-alone" rule; following it placed the coverage run (a default-features workspace nextest under the hood) AFTER the bindings regen, silently clobbering `pulse-app/ui/src/bindings/index.ts` back to the no-mcp shape between the regen-time grep verification and `git add` — commits 21d4de5/aae34e5 were pushed with no-mcp bindings (the defensive `use-mcp-delivery` hook kept tsc green by design, but `cargo xtask capability-drift` on those commits reports 3 missing `mcp.*` procedures → the CI gate is red on them). TWO amendments to the discipline: (1) ORDER — the regen-via-mcp-server-feature command (`cargo nextest run -p pulse-app --features mcp-server --bin pulse-app -E 'test(emit_taurpc_bindings)'`) is the absolute LAST cargo-adjacent step of any session: after nextest, after smoke checks, AND after `cargo llvm-cov` (the llvm-cov-last rule sequences cargo gates; the regen is post-cargo, not a cargo gate). (2) VERIFY THE STAGED COPY — after `git add`, gate the commit on `git show :pulse-app/ui/src/bindings/index.ts | grep -c '"mcp":'` ≥1 plus `cargo xtask capability-drift` clean; verifying the worktree at regen time is insufficient because any later default-features cargo op invalidates it silently. **[extended 2026-08-30: the staged read is now CODE — `capability-drift` itself asserts the staged bindings (full `EXPECTED_PROCEDURES` diff) + the staged capability grants (`check:staged-artifacts`, chunk 2026-08-30-staged-bindings-assertion), so the manual `git show` check is belt-and-braces rather than the only guard; the regen-then-stage ordering discipline is unchanged.]** The corrected bindings landed at the session-186 wrap commit. Generalizes: any generated-at-test-runtime artifact that rides commits (bindings, codegen snapshots) needs its freshness gate to read the INDEX (`git show :path`), not the worktree. **[corrected 2026-11-03: the `mcp-server` feature, its `mcp.*` router and the `andromeda-pulse-mcp` sidecar left at chunk `2026-11-03-stdio-sidecar-retired` — every regenerating op now writes the one bindings shape, so the no-mcp shape, the `--features mcp-server` regen and the `grep -c '"mcp":'` probe no longer exist; the order that stands is test-plan's per-chunk gate discipline (`capability-drift` before the workspace run, the featureless `emit_taurpc_bindings` regen last, `git diff --quiet {chunk-base} -- pulse-app/ui/src/bindings/index.ts` closing), green at chunk `2026-11-03-advisories-since-2026-10-12-closed`]**

- 2026-08-17: A COMBINED `cargo deny check bans licenses sources advisories` invocation can never be green in this project, so never list it that way as a chunk gate. The advisory posture is deliberate: a finding WITH a stated safe upgrade is never ignore-listed, so the owned set stays RED until upgraded — meaning `advisories` is a designed-red signal, not a pass/fail gate. Fold it into one command and the whole gate is permanently red, which (a) masks a genuine regression in `bans` / `licenses` / `sources`, and (b) trains the reader to ignore the result. Run them as TWO invocations: `cargo deny check bans licenses sources` is the pass/fail gate, and `cargo deny check advisories` is observed separately with its owned ID set enumerated in the chunk report so a NEW finding is distinguishable from the standing owned ones. The CI form at §Supply chain + CI already lists only `bans licenses sources` for exactly this reason; the gap this closes is chunk-PLAN authoring, where the combined form reads natural and slips into `## Test Commands`. Verified when a plan listed the combined form and the wrap had to split it to tell designed-red from regression. **[corrected 2026-11-03: `cargo deny check advisories` exits 0 (`advisories ok`) since chunk `2026-11-03-advisories-since-2026-10-12-closed` pruned the withdrawn GTK3 ignores and closed the owned set by upgrade, so it is no longer designed-red; the two-invocation split stays the safe form, since a new owned finding reddens `advisories` alone]**

- 2026-11-03: Before writing a `deny.toml [bans] skip` for a duplicate a bump surfaced, dry-run `cargo update -p {holder} --dry-run` for each holder of the OLD copy: an in-range update of one holder can drop the old copy whole, and a skip's «not source-fixable» clause is a measurement, never an assumption.

- 2026-05-13: `pulse-app/ui/src/bindings/index.ts` regenerates transiently on every `cargo nextest run --workspace --profile ci` (default features) AND every `cargo nextest run` invocation that hits the `emit_taurpc_bindings` test in `pulse-app/src/main.rs::tests`. Under default features the test's `.merge(...)` chain is cfg-gated to exclude the `mcp-server` namespace (per 2026-05-12 four-place-binding entry above + 2026-05-12 five-place cfg-gate entry below), so the emitted bindings.ts drops `mcp.start` / `mcp.status` / `mcp.stop` procedure references. The COMMITTED state of bindings.ts contains the full procedure set (last emitted with `--features mcp-server` enabled); subsequent default-features nextest runs LOCALLY overwrite the working tree copy. `cargo xtask capability-drift` reads bindings.ts and reports `drifted (3 missing: mcp.start, mcp.status, mcp.stop)` — confusing because EXPECTED_PROCEDURES IS correct + the four-place binding is in place; root cause is the transient working-tree overwrite. Resolution at wrap-session AND /implement Phase 2: `git checkout HEAD -- pulse-app/ui/src/bindings/index.ts` to restore the committed (full-set) state before re-running capability-drift OR before committing. Verified at chunks #51 + #52 wraps (3 regenerations across 2 sessions). Future wraps should expect this pattern AND restore bindings.ts after default-features test runs but BEFORE `cargo xtask capability-drift` invocation OR before staging files for commit. The committed state IS canonical; transient overwrites should not propagate to a commit. Generalizes to any future feature-gated TauRPC namespace (e.g., a hypothetical `--features otap-ingest` adding new procedures) — the same pattern would apply: default-features nextest drops them; restore via git checkout. **[corrected 2026-11-03: the `mcp-server` feature, its `mcp.*` router and the `andromeda-pulse-mcp` sidecar left at chunk `2026-11-03-stdio-sidecar-retired` — every regenerating op now writes the one bindings shape, so the no-mcp shape, the `--features mcp-server` regen and the `grep -c '"mcp":'` probe no longer exist; the order that stands is test-plan's per-chunk gate discipline (`capability-drift` before the workspace run, the featureless `emit_taurpc_bindings` regen last, `git diff --quiet {chunk-base} -- pulse-app/ui/src/bindings/index.ts` closing), green at chunk `2026-11-03-advisories-since-2026-10-12-closed`]**

- 2026-05-17: The 2026-05-13 entry above documents the recovery procedure `git checkout HEAD -- pulse-app/ui/src/bindings/index.ts` to restore the canonical full-set bindings.ts state. This recovery procedure RELIES ON HEAD itself containing the full-set canonical bindings.ts. If a prior wrap-session committed bindings.ts in default-features-overwrite state (chunk #59 wrap session 72 had this regression — commit 7d3207d's bindings.ts has no `mcp` namespace in ARGS_MAP), `git checkout HEAD -- pulse-app/ui/src/bindings/index.ts` restores the BROKEN state, not the canonical state; capability-drift remains drifted reporting 3 missing (mcp.start / mcp.status / mcp.stop). Resolution when HEAD is in broken state: regenerate freshly via `cargo nextest run -p pulse-app --features mcp-server -E 'test(emit_taurpc_bindings)'` (emits bindings.ts with all namespaces including `mcp.{start,status,stop}` via the cfg-gated `.merge(McpApiImpl)` chain) + stage the regenerated bindings.ts as part of the current chunk's commit (operational cleanup; not chunk-functional content). Pre-commit verification pattern at every wrap-session: `grep -c '"mcp":' pulse-app/ui/src/bindings/index.ts` MUST return ≥1 immediately before `git add` / `git commit`; if returns 0, regenerate via mcp-server-feature nextest before committing. Without this pre-commit verification, the regression auto-propagates: any future `cargo llvm-cov nextest --workspace` / default-features nextest run between regen + commit overwrites bindings.ts back to broken state, and the broken state gets committed unless wrap-session's final pre-commit check catches it. Verified this session (#74 chunk #60 wrap) where /implement Phase 2 mcp-server regen + capability-drift-clean was undone by the subsequent llvm-cov coverage run; pre-commit re-regen + verification was the final fix. Pattern recurs on every chunk wrap involving any default-features nextest invocation between regen + commit — treat as standard wrap-session discipline, not chunk-specific. **[corrected 2026-11-03: the `mcp-server` feature, its `mcp.*` router and the `andromeda-pulse-mcp` sidecar left at chunk `2026-11-03-stdio-sidecar-retired` — every regenerating op now writes the one bindings shape, so the no-mcp shape, the `--features mcp-server` regen and the `grep -c '"mcp":'` probe no longer exist; the order that stands is test-plan's per-chunk gate discipline (`capability-drift` before the workspace run, the featureless `emit_taurpc_bindings` regen last, `git diff --quiet {chunk-base} -- pulse-app/ui/src/bindings/index.ts` closing), green at chunk `2026-11-03-advisories-since-2026-10-12-closed`]**

- 2026-05-22 (session 119): When a `pulse-app/tests/*.rs` integration test spawns a SIBLING-crate binary as a subprocess via `tokio::process::Command::new(target/debug/<binary>)` (e.g., chunk #77 `security_mcp_response_body_redaction.rs` spawns `andromeda-pulse-mcp` from the `mcp-server` crate; chunk #50 `e2e_p3_mcp_subprocess_tools_call.rs` does the same), `cargo nextest run -p pulse-app --features mcp-server -E binary(<test>)` does NOT auto-build the sibling-crate binary. The test panics at spawn time with `Os { code: 2, kind: NotFound, message: "The system cannot find the file specified." }`. Resolution: explicitly run `cargo build -p mcp-server --features mcp-server --bin andromeda-pulse-mcp` BEFORE the nextest invocation. CI workflow should sequence the build step before the feature-gated subprocess-test nextest invocation. Verified at chunk #77 /implement Phase 2 when test (c) MCP response body redaction failed on first invocation; explicit build + retry succeeded (2/2 passing). Pairs naturally with the 2026-05-13 binary-path-resolution entry (CARGO_BIN_EXE_<name> not accessible cross-crate; derive path from CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR + ../target/debug/<binary>) — together those two entries form the complete cross-crate subprocess-test discipline. Generalizes to any future feature-gated subprocess test wherein the spawned binary lives in a different workspace crate (chunk #82+ LLM runtime sidecar tests will likely follow the same shape). **[corrected 2026-11-03: its example left — `andromeda-pulse-mcp` and the `mcp-server` feature were retired at chunk `2026-11-03-stdio-sidecar-retired`; the rule (nextest does not build a sibling crate's binary) stands for any test that spawns one]**

- 2026-05-25 (session 150): EXTENSION to the 2026-05-13 + 2026-05-17 bindings.ts regen discipline — when invoking the regen-via-mcp-server-feature nextest, prefer `cargo nextest run -p pulse-app --features mcp-server --bin pulse-app -E 'test(emit_taurpc_bindings)'` over the simpler `-E 'test(emit_taurpc_bindings)'` filter. Rationale: cargo nextest's filter applies AFTER compilation, so any pulse-app integration test target that fails to build (e.g., `pulse-app/tests/e2e_drain_template_assignment.rs` failing with `libduckdb_sys` rlib-format mismatch under a specific feature combination) blocks the targeted regen invocation even when the bin-target's emit_taurpc_bindings test is the only ACTUAL test being run. Adding `--bin pulse-app` restricts compilation to the bin target ONLY (which contains the emit_taurpc_bindings test in main.rs::tests), sidestepping unrelated rlib-format errors in sibling integration test crates. Discovered at chunk #86 wrap (session 150) when the regen invocation hit `error: crate libduckdb_sys required to be available in rlib format, but was not found in this form` against e2e_drain_template_assignment compilation despite the regen test living elsewhere. The fix takes ≤5 seconds; the rlib-format root cause is environmental (target/.fingerprint inconsistency between feature combinations); the workaround is durable across chunk + feature-flag boundary changes. Apply pre-emptively whenever rerunning the regen-via-mcp-server-feature path post bindings.ts-overwriting test invocations. **[corrected 2026-11-03: the `mcp-server` feature, its `mcp.*` router and the `andromeda-pulse-mcp` sidecar left at chunk `2026-11-03-stdio-sidecar-retired` — every regenerating op now writes the one bindings shape, so the no-mcp shape, the `--features mcp-server` regen and the `grep -c '"mcp":'` probe no longer exist; the order that stands is test-plan's per-chunk gate discipline (`capability-drift` before the workspace run, the featureless `emit_taurpc_bindings` regen last, `git diff --quiet {chunk-base} -- pulse-app/ui/src/bindings/index.ts` closing), green at chunk `2026-11-03-advisories-since-2026-10-12-closed`]**

- 2026-06-28: `cargo nextest run -p {crate} -E 'binary(X) + binary(Y)'` (and `--workspace`) narrows what RUNS, not what COMPILES — nextest compiles ALL of the crate's test binaries (the pulse-app suite is ~30) before the `-E` filter selects which to run. On a memory-tight host that parallel compile can rustc-OOM (`memory allocation of N bytes failed`, often cascading into the session-163/183 rlib/ICE signatures across the sibling binaries) even when only 2 binaries are wanted. Remedies: (a) to compile ONLY the wanted binaries, `cargo test --test X --test Y -p pulse-app` (libtest; the 2026-05-31 session-153 path-(a)) — compiles just those; (b) when the full suite IS wanted, throttle parallel rustc + disable incremental: `cargo build --workspace --tests --jobs 4 && cargo nextest run --workspace --profile ci` (build-first de-races per session-165; nextest then just runs the pre-built binaries; `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0` exported for the session avoids the 183 corruption). Verified at chunk 2026-06-28-deterministic-env-gated-l4-mode: a plain `cargo nextest run -p pulse-app -E 'binary(...)'` OOM'd compiling the 30-binary set right after a SUCCESSFUL `cargo build -p pulse-app`; `cargo clean -p pulse-app` + `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0` + `cargo test --test` ran the 2 wanted binaries green, then `--jobs 4` carried the full workspace suite (1681) green. Extends the rlib-race family (150/153/163/165/183) with the compile-parallelism-OOM facet + the "-E filters RUN not COMPILE" insight. **[extended 2026-08-29]** The same memory-pressure class has a SECOND presentation that does not look like memory at all: `error: could not exec the linker rust-lld.exe — Insufficient quota to complete the requested service. (os error 1453)` — a linker SPAWN failure during the parallel link burst, on a WARM target (no cold rebuild involved). It reads like a broken toolchain or a permissions fault; it is the host refusing the process spawn under commit/paging pressure while several rust-lld instances run at once. Same remedy as the OOM facet, applied verbatim: `cargo build --workspace --tests --jobs 4` first, then `cargo nextest run --workspace --profile ci` over the pre-built binaries — green on the first retry at `2026-08-29-halo-state-pulse-signature-deferred` (2077/2077). Recognize 1453 as this family before reinstalling anything. **[extended 2026-08-29b — two MORE presentations, both measured at `2026-08-29-advisory-backlog`.]** (c) **Commit-limit during the feature-graph link set:** `exit code: 0xc000012d` (STATUS_COMMITMENT_LIMIT) on a test-binary link plus `failed to mmap file ... The paging file is too small for this operation to complete. (os error 1455)` on rlib metadata reads, CASCADING as `E0786 found invalid metadata` / `E0463 can't find crate` across sibling binaries — reads like corrupted artifacts or a broken crate graph; it is the same commit/paging pressure, hit when `cargo nextest run -p pulse-app --features mcp-server -E 'binary(X)'` compiles ALL ~30 test binaries under the feature graph. Same `--build-jobs 4` remedy, green on retry. (d) **Disk-full is a DISTINCT class with a distinct remedy:** `LLVM ERROR: IO failure on output stream: no space on device` during link — `target/` ACCUMULATES artifact generations across months of chunks (measured 268G, deps alone 217G; two wasmtime majors coexisting after a bump); the throttle does NOT help this one. Remedy: `cargo clean` (operator pre-authorized) — freed 290 GiB; the cold rebuild steady-states around ~66G. Check `df` before pattern-matching a link failure to the memory family: 100M free and 100% used is class (d), not (a)-(c). **[extended 2026-08-30]** The session env-prefix is part of cargo's FINGERPRINT, so EVERY cargo invocation of the session must carry it — `cargo nextest list` included: one list invocation without `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0`, minutes after a green suite, re-fingerprinted the workspace and burst-rebuilt unthrottled, presenting as rust-lld `0xc000001d` + an E0463 cascade (this family's fourth presentation); the remedy was the standing one applied verbatim — re-run `cargo build --workspace --tests --jobs 4` under the SAME env, then list under that env. **[corrected 2026-11-03: the `mcp-server` feature named here left at chunk `2026-11-03-stdio-sidecar-retired` (`pulse-app/Cargo.toml [features]` holds `default` and `otap-ingest`); the mechanism stands for any second feature graph]**

- 2026-07-02: DISK-HYGIENE ROUTINE — low disk before a build/smoke on this host → `scripts\free-disk.ps1`. Safe-by-default: no args = MEASURE + dry-run (deletes nothing); `-Execute` deletes. It reclaims REGENERABLE-only artifacts (`target\debug\incremental`, `<cargo-home>\registry\{cache,src}`, `target\doc`, the gitignored `experiments\llamacpp_spike\target`, and `%APPDATA%\andromeda-pulse\logs\agent-latest.jsonl.*` older than 2 days by `LastWriteTime`) and NEVER touches `target\debug\deps` (warm current-toolchain artifacts), the corpus/DB, `.andromeda\`, `ui\dist`, `registry\index`, source, or the last-2-days logs (which hold the F7/display-truth smoke telemetry the wrap curates — `item_count` / `state_distribution`). USAGE CONSTRAINT — an agent CANNOT run `-Execute` (PowerShell / recursive-`rm` deny rules); the loop is: agent runs the default dry-run to MEASURE → hands the user `powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts\free-disk.ps1 -Execute` → user reclaims → agent re-runs the dry-run to VERIFY freed space + preserve-list intact. DEEPER lever after toolchain churn (safe — keeps current warm): `cargo install cargo-sweep ; cargo sweep --installed` removes ONLY uninstalled-toolchain artifacts — observed to reclaim ~nothing (11.97 MiB) on a host where all 7 toolchains are still installed (the 97G `target\debug\deps` is warm current-toolchain artifacts, correctly preserved). AVOID `cargo sweep --time N` by default (drops stable-but-old deps → partial rebuild + OOM risk). Pairs with the 2026-06-12 llvm-cov-disk sequencing entry (llvm-cov builds a SECOND full instrumented workspace — sequence it last-and-alone). Verified 2026-07-02: dry-run measured cleanly, `-Execute` reclaimed ~8G on D: (44G→51.9G free) with the full preserve-list intact. **[extended 2026-08-22]** Know the FAILURE SIGNATURE and the bigger lever: disk exhaustion during a Rust build surfaces as `LLVM ERROR: IO failure on output stream: no space on device` from `rust-lld` — a linker error, not a disk error — and it fires at LINK time, so it lands after a long compile rather than up front. When it hits, `free-disk.ps1`'s reclaimable set may be far too small (measured ~13G against a 300G/100%-full drive); the effective lever is the pre-authorized `cargo clean -p pulse-app`, which freed **93.2 GiB** in one step because ~30 pulse-app test binaries each carry a large `.exe` + `.pdb` in `target/debug/deps`. Prefer the targeted `-p` clean over a full `cargo clean`: it keeps every dependency rlib warm, so the rebuild is minutes rather than a full cold cycle. **[extended 2026-08-26] Re-measure free space with PowerShell, not `df`, immediately after the clean — and do it before concluding the reclaim was insufficient.** Reproduced the whole signature again (D: at 2.6G/300G, `target/` 180G, the ENOSPC buried under a ~15KB linker-argument dump where a short `tail` cannot see it; `cargo clean -p pulse-app` removed 11,867 files / **87.6 GiB**). The new facet: seconds after that delete, MSYS `df -h /d` reported **29G** free while PowerShell `Get-PSDrive D` reported **87.5 GB** — ReFS reclaim was still settling and `df` had cached. Acting on `df` alone reads as "the remedy freed far less than the ~87G of artifacts about to be rebuilt" and escalates for disk that is already free; both agreed at ~88G on re-read. Treat PowerShell as authoritative for free space on this ReFS Dev Drive, and re-read after any large delete. **[extended 2026-08-29] A `--features` build is a SECOND native compile, so the targeted `-p` clean can be the wrong lever.** Cargo fingerprints per feature graph, so `cargo build -p mcp-server --features mcp-server` rebuilds the whole `libduckdb-sys` C++ tree from scratch rather than reusing the default-features one — two full DuckDB compiles must fit at once. Measured at `2026-08-29-app-registry-reconciliation`: `cargo clean -p pulse-app` freed **97.4 GiB**, and the feature build exhausted the drive again minutes later, this time surfacing as `cl.exe : fatal error C1085: Cannot write compiler generated file … No space left on device` (the cc-rs sibling of the `rust-lld` signature above — same cause, different tool, and likewise buried under a multi-KB argument dump). `target/debug` had reached **301.6 GB on a 300 GB drive**. The lever that worked was the pre-authorized FULL `cargo clean` (**310.1 GiB**, 266.8 GB free after), then rebuilding once on the feature graph and running the remaining verification there. **Decision rule: if the session still owes a `--features` build, budget for two native compiles — a targeted `-p` clean buys one, and paying the cold-rebuild cost once beats discovering it mid-gate.** The ~20 s ReFS reclaim lag applied to both deletes. **[corrected 2026-11-03: the `mcp-server` feature named here left at chunk `2026-11-03-stdio-sidecar-retired` (`pulse-app/Cargo.toml [features]` holds `default` and `otap-ingest`); the mechanism stands for any second feature graph]**

- 2026-08-15: EXTENSION to the bindings.ts regen family (2026-05-13 / 2026-05-17 here, plus the 2026-06-12 staged-copy entry in `rules/security.md`) — the facet none of them cover: **the wrap's own P7 light gate is structurally a default-features cargo op, and it ALWAYS runs AFTER P2's regen.** So the regen being "the last cargo-adjacent step" of /implement is not sufficient: the wrap re-runs the chunk's Test Commands (which include `cargo nextest run --workspace`) and that rewrites `pulse-app/ui/src/bindings/index.ts` to the no-mcp shape all over again, between the regen and `git add`. Discipline for any wrap whose chunk touches TauRPC: (a) re-run the regen (`cargo nextest run -p pulse-app --features mcp-server --bin pulse-app -E 'test(emit_taurpc_bindings)'`) AFTER the light gate, before staging; (b) gate the commit on the STAGED copy, not the worktree — `git show :pulse-app/ui/src/bindings/index.ts | grep -c '"mcp":'` must be ≥1, since the worktree can be correct while the index carries the clobbered version; (c) re-check `cargo xtask capability-drift` after the LAST cargo op of the session, whatever it is. **[extended 2026-08-30: (b) and (c) are now one mechanical step — `capability-drift` itself runs the staged assertion (bindings + capability grants vs their pins, chunk 2026-08-30-staged-bindings-assertion), so running it LAST checks the index copy by construction; the manual grep remains valid as a quick pre-stage probe.]** **[corrected 2026-09-30: (a) and (c) no longer hold as written — `capability-drift` now runs BEFORE the default-features workspace nextest, and the mcp-server regen plus a chunk-base `git diff --quiet` bindings probe close every plan's gate block, so the light gate re-runs the regen itself (test-plan §3; operator-ratified; both runs at 2026-09-30-dual-license closed exit 0).]** (Origin: the `b08e10a` wrap's near-miss — drift appeared only in the staged copy after the light gate rewrote bindings, and was caught by luck rather than by the check order.) **[corrected 2026-11-03: the `mcp-server` feature, its `mcp.*` router and the `andromeda-pulse-mcp` sidecar left at chunk `2026-11-03-stdio-sidecar-retired` — every regenerating op now writes the one bindings shape, so the no-mcp shape, the `--features mcp-server` regen and the `grep -c '"mcp":'` probe no longer exist; the order that stands is test-plan's per-chunk gate discipline (`capability-drift` before the workspace run, the featureless `emit_taurpc_bindings` regen last, `git diff --quiet {chunk-base} -- pulse-app/ui/src/bindings/index.ts` closing), green at chunk `2026-11-03-advisories-since-2026-10-12-closed`]**

- 2026-11-03: A gate probe that greps a source tree holding a committed GENERATED artifact (the TauRPC bindings) reads that artifact's committed copy, stale until the regenerating entry runs — order such a probe AFTER the regen, or keep the artifact out of its scope.

title: 2026-11-03 — A `git diff` scope guard cannot read a recorded companion

data.head: ## 2026-11-03 — A `git diff` scope guard cannot read a recorded companion

body: A plan's scope-guard entry written as `git diff --name-only {base} -- {dirs}`, with research's file list as its exclusions, reads every changed file outside that list as out of scope — including one the operator recorded as a companion in the chunk's scope record, which the guard never reads. `gate.py scope` reads the scope record and is the authoritative scope read: a plan either excludes recorded companions from its guard or lets `gate.py scope` stand as the scope gate. Where it applies: any chunk whose scope record gains a companion after research listed the files.

title: Gate ORDER around the committed GENERATED bindings (`pulse-app/ui/src/bindings/index.ts`, rewritten to the no-mcp shape
body:
- pattern: Gate ORDER around the committed GENERATED bindings (`pulse-app/ui/src/bindings/index.ts`, rewritten to the no-mcp shape by every default-features `cargo nextest` / `cargo run` through `taurpc`'s `export_types()`) — in a chunk plan's `## Test Commands` and so in the P7 light gate that re-runs that block.
  verdict: routine
  note: routine-ORDERING (a check, not a judgment). `cargo xtask capability-drift` runs BEFORE the default-features `cargo nextest run --workspace`, while the worktree bindings are still the committed mcp shape; the `--features mcp-server` `emit_taurpc_bindings` regen follows that workspace run as the LAST cargo-adjacent step; a probe named against the chunk base closes the sequence, `git diff --quiet <chunk-base> -- pulse-app/ui/src/bindings/index.ts` (exit 0 = the bindings end byte-identical to the base). The staged half stays in the gate itself (`check:staged-artifacts`, folded into `capability-drift`, reads the git index, which no cargo run touches). Scope: the base-identity close was measured for a chunk adding no TauRPC procedure. A chunk that CHANGES the procedure set closes instead with: the `--features mcp-server` regen after the workspace run → two content probes on the worktree bindings (the new procedure's name; `grep -c '"mcp":'` ≥ 1) → `git add` of the regenerated bindings WITH the `EXPECTED_PROCEDURES` pin (index only, no commit) → `check:staged-artifacts`, then `capability-drift` LAST (both read the staged copy; before the regen the committed bindings lack the pinned procedure, so drift cannot run earlier). The regen must also PRECEDE the `ui/dist` build and every release build a live leg drives: the taurpc proxy resolves methods against the `ARGS_MAP` bundled into `ui/dist`, so a dist built before the regen ships without the new method and a fire-and-forget caller no-ops silently (measured at 2026-09-30-perf-instruments-measure-their-budgets: 1 bundle occurrence vs 2). That procedure-changing close was first run at that chunk and replaced this rule's former "not yet specified — escalate that case until one is" clause on the operator's approval at its wrap (overseer: "one rule sharpened in place replaces its escalate clause; a sibling would leave two rules on one subject"). Provenance: the overseer's founder-delegated directive of 2026-09-30 (not a founder ruling), first run at 2026-09-30-dual-license and approved as this rule at its wrap; it answers the every-chunk recurrence of the bindings being rewritten before `capability-drift` read them, which the LAST ordering of the rule it supersedes produced. test-plan §3 Per-chunk gate discipline states the same order.
